outcome: THRESHOLD B REDUCED FROM 3 TO 2. DB-5 and PV-3 closed on evidence. MO-1 and BR-2 both require a product-owner action that §292 is forbidden to take on the owner's behalf. THRESHOLD B DOES NOT CLOSE.

DB_5.reconciliation: The §291 report was internally inconsistent — prose said 'now fail-closed' while the return listed DB-5 as NEW and not repaired, and the register said OPEN. Reconciling it found something worse than an inconsistent report.
DB_5.defectInTheRepairItself: §291 added an OPTIONAL `scope` parameter and returned early when it was absent. The query underneath was NEVER scoped. So the guard held only because no caller passed a scope, and would have become FAIL-OPEN the moment one did: the caller would believe it had asked for one workspace and would receive every workspace. A guard that inverts when someone starts using it is worse than no guard, because it reads as protection.
DB_5.correction: The parameter is removed. There is no way to ASK for cross-tenant data, because there is nothing to ask with.
DB_5.whyNotProperlyScoped: fix_feedback has no owner column, and its report_id is not reliably a report — OutcomeService writes a corrective ACTION id into it. No correct predicate exists over this schema, and §292 does not authorise the migration that would create one.
